data.name: Music platform monitoring
data.prompt:
Run the combined MUSIC-platform marketing-analysis queue under Z:\My Songs\Reports\music-platform-monitoring using the current Europe/London date. The single controller now covers twelve profiles: Spotify, Amazon Music for Artists, Apple Music for Artists and Shazam, YouTube Studio, Meta/Instagram, Google Search Console, website conversion, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, cross-platform release presence, and a monthly Deezer/TIDAL/SoundCloud/Bandcamp audit. Amazon is explicitly resumed inside this queue by Kieran's 2 November 2026 instruction; its old standalone automation stays paused to prevent duplicate wakeups.

Quiet blogworthiness record: before finishing, record Blogworthiness: PASS or FAIL with a short evidence-based reason and source evidence in the existing report or final handoff. For PASS also record the reader-interest angle, duplicate check and next action. Do not send or surface a standalone completion-check reminder.

Scheduled-job browser access — Kieran, 28 October 2026: This scheduled job is explicitly authorised to use the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in in-app browser (`@Browser`) whenever it is useful for its existing authorised work. This supersedes any older prompt or AGENTS.md rule that disables or limits the in-app browser for this scheduled job. Prefer a sufficient connector/API/CLI when it is more reliable; browser access does not add authority for sends, publication, account changes, spending, rights commitments or sensitive disclosure. Reuse or open only the tabs needed, preserve other owners' tabs and unsaved work, close completed job-created or released borrowed tabs, and verify a fresh browser-tab inventory before handoff. If `@Browser` is unavailable in the scheduled run, record the precise capability hold; do not claim access or completion and do not switch to native whole-PC control.

Browser repair requirement — Kieran, 2 November 2026: If the intended browser route is unavailable, disconnected, stale or otherwise broken, diagnose and repair that same supported route before declaring a hold. Follow the maintained Browser setup and troubleshooting workflow, re-establish the browser binding or tab as applicable, retry the original authenticated dashboard, and verify the repair on the intended page. Do not replace missing control-panel evidence with public estimates, stale snapshots, search results, native whole-PC control, or another browser family. Do not restart or terminate Codex or a browser, alter security/account settings, or enter credentials automatically; if supported recovery reaches a genuine user sign-in, extension-connection, security, or explicit restart boundary, preserve the exact checkpoint and report the smallest required action. After repair, continue the original analysis and perform verified tab cleanup.

Read Z:\My Songs\AGENTS.md, manifest.json, guide.html and shared-analysis-baseline.txt first. The shared baseline carries the strongest compatible analysis features from all profiles and must be applied in full to every attempted profile without replacing its specialist checks. The authoritative instructions for every migrated or queue-native profile are retained in its profile.json and instructions.txt. Their complete checks, reporting obligations, report destinations, daily/weekly/monthly recurrence, account/action restrictions and notification preferences remain in force. Current project rules override older routing wording, especially the in-app-browser prohibition. Consolidation is not permission to omit or reduce a monitor's checks.

Use C:\Python314\python.exe with monitor.py in this folder. Start with `due`. If empty, end without account access or a repetitive report. If work is due, run `claim --owner <current CODEX_THREAD_ID>`. At most TWO profiles are selected; process them sequentially within the returned 45-minute deadline. A shared lease coordinates this controller with Song marketing operations. When a shared lease is busy, retain all due work and end; never start a second browser/account sweep or wake another chat. No subagents. An existing own lease is also a hold, regardless of age. Read its exact owner metadata. Only after supported chat tools verify the exact owner idle/stopped may that owner's adapter run `recover --token <token> --verified-owner-idle <exact-owner-id>`. Do not break an active lease or infer inactivity from elapsed time.

Before each selected monitor, verify its instructions SHA-256 and read the FULL original instructions, its referenced workflow/Potential problems guidance, newest report and current same-date report. Keep all original report and evidence folders; append/reconcile one coherent report per platform and London date. Do not replace the full checks with a summary or treat a partial pass as complete. Retain an explicit per-profile list of completed, blocked and remaining required checks in its checkpoint. If any required check remains unattempted or incomplete, record partial, with its exact remaining-check list, and resume that list on a later pass. The queue retains partial obligations and retries after four hours with fair ordering. Deadline/batch limits bound a pass, not the total checks retained.

Preserve Spotify release/upcoming/pitch-ownership and 24h/7d/28d checks; YouTube's complete released-song inventory, auditable full-upload/Short component totals, retention, comments and every other source check; Meta's complete analytics surfaces, public profile/bio-link checks and labelled cross-platform comparisons; Search Console's performance, indexing, sitemap, video and site-health surfaces and KeywordMoves evidence; TikTok's 7d/28d metrics, preceding-period comparisons, post/audience/retention/search analysis; and the catalogue audit's complete distributor/artist/released/future/public-store/control-panel/playback distinctions. These examples do not replace any paragraph in the source profiles. Preserve Amazon's complete profile and run it when selected; Kieran explicitly enabled it on 2 November 2026. Also preserve Apple/Shazam discovery, website funnel and outbound-event definitions, X and LinkedIn native metric definitions, and per-platform Deezer/TIDAL/SoundCloud/Bandcamp access and catalogue distinctions.

Use source-specific connectors/APIs/CLI when supported, the permitted external Chrome extension for genuine signed-in interaction, and bounded isolated signed-out checks only for their actual scope. The in-app browser is explicitly re-enabled for this scheduled job under the 28 October 2026 rule. No credential creation, consent/access change, paid operation or account mutation is newly authorised. Preserve each source profile's read-only or exact-action gates, including any existing limited standing permission. Reuse source-native observations only when their account, scope, reporting window, cutoff and timestamp actually match; otherwise label them historical/supplemental or unavailable. Never turn a dash into zero, substitute public estimates for control-panel data, compare unlike windows as matched cohorts, count scheduled/private assets as public, or infer campaign causality/outcomes.

Complete the original KeywordMoves/register, verified-publicity, EPK and evidence follow-through where that source actually requires it and the existing permissions allow it. Keep private evidence and user-controlled media in their established locations. Preserve exact song/artist/master associations, mandatory send claims and action approvals, current WordPress REST/timing/mobile verification and future-publication gates. No new campaign asset, render, model download, broad scan, subscription, posting or outreach follows merely from consolidation.

Mandatory self-improvement and five-action output — Kieran, 2 November 2026: Every attempted profile must include a `Self-improvement loop` section that reviews the newest compatible report and current analytical process, identifies at least one concrete low-risk improvement, implements every justified in-scope improvement in the same run, and records the gap, change, verification, comparability effect and remaining work; never invent a change. It must also include `Five immediately actionable items` with exactly five numbered, prioritized, evidence-backed actions or genuine repair/instrumentation/data-access prerequisites. Each item must name the affected platform/account and asset, exact next action, evidence, why now, expected outcome, primary metric/window, owner/access/cost assumptions, risk/confounder and review date. Review the prior five items' verified status first. The list is analysis, not new authority to publish, send, edit accounts, spend or bypass any gate.

After every attempted profile, update its original report/checkpoint and run `record --token <token> --profile <id> --outcome completed|blocked|partial|no_action --evidence <real-report-or-checkpoint-path> --note <precise-state>`. Completed requires all original required checks accounted for; blocked must identify each genuinely inaccessible required surface. Partial retains unfinished work. Also update latest-evidence.json with platform/account identity, report/evidence paths and hashes, actual observation time, data window/cutoff, completion/access state, remaining checks and public/private limits. Never call an unavailable or historical observation fresh. Song campaigns may reuse this index as labelled evidence; do not make them re-fetch the same dashboard by default.

Before the deadline, checkpoint and run `release --token <token>` in cleanup even if selected work was deferred. Close completed job-created/released borrowed browser tabs through supported controls and verify cleanup. Preserve unsaved forms/uploads with a precise hold. Do not kill/restart Codex, move databases, interrupt another job, alter other schedules or disturb video renders. Report useful findings, changed blockers or required decisions concisely; keep routine coordination private. No run, completed check, delivery, publication, adoption by another chat or crash repair is proved by saved configuration or synthetic tests.
